verdicts.title: Rail and footer surface assertions pass against a transparent parent
verdicts.section: Task 5: The three loaded-player shots — Step 3 (the surfaceDiffersFromParent helper) and Step 5 (its own proof)
verdicts.contradicts: Feasibility's variant of this same fix (walk up to the nearest painting ancestor AND rename the helper to surfaceDiffersFromBackdrop) collides with F-3's guard anchors if those name the old identifier. Resolved: take the document.body comparison (already spiked by the orchestrator) and give F-3 helper-name-agnostic anchors, so the two fixes are independent.
verdicts.spike: Carried forward as CONFIRMED per the orchestrator: both parents paint nothing (.nh-drop-zone has only a [data-dragging] rule; the footer's parent is <div className="shrink-0" data-testid="player-status">), and the document.body fix gives vsParent=true/vsBody=true for a distinct rail versus vsParent=true/vsBody=FALSE for a rail regressed to the page background. I separately confirmed the mechanism in a browser probe: a transparent element computes backgroundColor 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)', so any opaque own colour differs from it.
verdicts.whats_wrong: The helper compares an element's background against its immediate parent's, but both parents paint nothing, so the computed parent colour is always 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' and any opaque own colour differs from it. The assertion can never fail, and Task 5 Step 5's prescribed proof (swap bg-rail for bg-background and expect a FAIL) will pass.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename the helper to surfaceDiffersFromPageBackground and have it compare the element's computed background-color against document.body's instead of el.parentElement's, updating the two call sites in the bundled-beat shot and the Task 5 Interfaces line; leave Step 5's two proofs worded exactly as they are, because with this helper they now fail as written.
verdicts.why_it_works: body is the only element between the page and these two surfaces that actually paints, and it paints the very token (--background) that a regressed rail or footer would fall back to — so own === backdrop and the assertion goes red exactly when the surface flattens.
verdicts.scenario: You are adding the screenshot test for the player screen. The plan tells you to check that the left rail still has its own shade of grey, and then to prove the check really works by making the rail the same colour as the page behind it and watching the check fail. It does not fail. It passes, because the check compares the rail against a see-through box wrapped around it rather than against the page. You are left holding a check that cannot catch the thing it was written for, and a step in the plan you cannot complete.

verdicts.title: Ghost-hover poll compares the hover to its own transparent resting value
verdicts.section: Task 6: The hover and breakpoint shots — Step 1 (the ghost-hover shot) and Step 4 (its proof)
verdicts.contradicts: The fix as FILED by adversarial (compare the hovered value against the rail's background) does not contradict another section, but my spike shows it does not catch the regression the plan's own comment names — hover:bg-muted differs from the rail, so it would pass. My after-text replaces it with the token-equality form, which honours the plan's own 'both values through the SAME serializer' rule in the Task 5 helper doc-comment and does not conflict with F-1's document.body fix (different call site, and the two assertions genuinely need different shapes).
verdicts.spike: Ran a real Chromium probe on Playwright 1.61.1 with the repo's own token values and Tailwind v4's real preflight rule (web/node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css:236-252 sets button { background-color: transparent }). Resting is 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' in all three cases. The plan's `hovered !== resting` PASSES for hover:bg-elevate (correct), hover:bg-muted (the named regression) AND hover:bg-rail (Step 4's own sabotage) — fully vacuous. 'hovered !== rail' catches bg-rail but still passes bg-muted. 'hovered === var(--elevate) read through a throwaway element' is the only form that discriminates: elevate PASS, muted FAIL, rail FAIL, and the token read comes back 'oklch(0.935 0.006 240.4)', character-identical to the hovered computed value.
verdicts.whats_wrong: The ghost button paints no background at rest (client/src/components/ui/Button/Button.tsx:36-37 gives the variant only hover:bg-elevate and aria-expanded:bg-elevate), and Tailwind's preflight makes every <button> transparent, so `resting` is always 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'. Any opaque hover colour differs from it, so the poll passes under both regressions — including the one Step 4 tells the implementer to plant and expect a failure from.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Drop the `resting` read and assert the hovered background EQUALS --elevate resolved through the same computed-style serializer (a throwaway element carrying background-color: var(--elevate)), and change Step 4's sabotage from hover:bg-rail to hover:bg-muted so the proof plants the regression the shot's own comment names.
verdicts.why_it_works: Spiked: token-equality is the only form that fails for both hover:bg-muted and hover:bg-rail while passing the correct hover:bg-elevate, and reading the token through a throwaway element returns the identical serialization, so the comparison cannot go green on a format mismatch.
verdicts.scenario: You are adding the screenshot of a button on the left rail with the mouse resting on it. The plan tells you to prove its colour check works by making the hover colour identical to the rail, so the highlight disappears, then watch the check fail. It passes instead. The button has no colour at all until the mouse arrives, so "the hovered colour is different from the resting colour" is true for every colour you could possibly pick — including both of the broken ones.

verdicts.title: Task 8 hook guard is vacuous for three of the four surface assertions
verdicts.section: Task 8: Guard that the pixel lane actually compares pixels — Step 2 (the hook loop) and Step 4 (proof 4)
verdicts.contradicts: none — and deliberately so: I made the anchors helper-name-agnostic (`(page, 'player-rail')` rather than `surfaceDiffersFromParent(page, …)`) precisely so this fix survives F-1's rename whether or not F-1 lands. The fix moves in the same direction as F-4's (anchor to the real construct, never a bare substring) and reintroduces none of F-4's problem, because these are presence checks on code, not absence checks over YAML comments.
verdicts.spike: Assembled the plan's prescribed pages.vr.ts from its own fenced blocks (Tasks 4-7, minus the two prints the plan says to delete) and ran the guard's `sources.some(src => src.includes(hook))` verbatim, then deleted each surface assertion in turn. Only transport-row makes the guard bite — 1 of 4 load-bearing. player-rail survives in the snapshot name 'player-rail-ghost-hover.png'; open-file-button survives in `const ghost = page.getByTestId('open-file-button')`, which the hover needs anyway; engine-error survives in `const panel = page.getByTestId('engine-error')`, in 'player-engine-error.png' and in two prose comments. The `backgroundColor` arm also stays green after deleting any single poll. I then verified four replacement anchors are each unique in the prescribed file and match none of the false positives (snapshot filename, bare locator, prose comment).
verdicts.whats_wrong: Three of the four names the guard searches for also occur in the same file for reasons unrelated to their surface assertion, so deleting those three assertions leaves the guard green — and Task 8 Step 4's fourth proof, which the plan calls the reason Task 8 exists, prints PASS instead of the quoted failure.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Replace the four bare-id presence checks with one regex per surface assertion, each anchored to that assertion's own expression — `(page, 'player-rail')`, `(page, 'transport-row')`, `var(--elevate)` and `'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'` — and reword Task 8 Step 4's fourth proof to quote the new message.
verdicts.why_it_works: Spiked: each of those four strings occurs exactly once in the prescribed shot file, inside the assertion it guards, and none is produced by a snapshot filename, a locator the shot needs anyway, or a prose comment — so deleting any one assertion now turns the guard red.
verdicts.scenario: You are adding the safety net that fails the build if someone later deletes one of the four colour checks. The plan tells you to test it by removing the left rail's check and watching the build turn red. It stays green. Three of the four names the net looks for also appear elsewhere in the very same file — once in a screenshot's filename, twice in lines the tests need for a different reason — so the net only notices when the fourth one goes.

verdicts.title: The web-job guard forbids a phrase the job's own comment carries
verdicts.section: Task 9: Move web/'s whole browser lane into the container — Step 1 (the job YAML) versus Step 7 (the guard) and Step 8 (its expected result)
verdicts.contradicts: none. It is the same direction as F-3's fix (anchor to a real construct), and it reintroduces nothing of F-3's vacuity problem: F-3 is a presence check that must not be satisfiable by prose, this is an absence check that must not be TRIPPED by prose. Both are satisfied by anchoring to the real line.
verdicts.spike: Carried forward as CONFIRMED per the orchestrator (plan line 1561 carries the phrase inside the web job's comment; plan line 1719 forbids it inside the sliced job, and the slice includes comments). I additionally tested both regexes against the plan's prescribed web-job YAML: /playwright install/ matches (guard RED on the comment), /^\s+run:.*playwright install/m does not match (guard GREEN, comment kept), and the anchored form still matches a real step line ('      run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium').
verdicts.whats_wrong: The guard asserts the string 'playwright install' appears nowhere in the sliced web job, but that job's own Install-deps comment ends with 'no `playwright install`'. So `pnpm run test:tooling` goes red the moment Task 9 lands, contradicting Step 8's stated 'Expected: all PASS', with a message pointing at an install step that does not exist.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Anchor the assertion to a real run line — /^\s+run:.*playwright install/m — and leave the job comment exactly as written.
verdicts.why_it_works: The anchored pattern can only match a YAML run: value, so the explanatory comment passes while an actual install step still fails; it is the same anchoring rationale this test already states two assertions above it.
verdicts.scenario: You have just moved the web tests into their own build job and you run the repo's own checks, which the plan says should all pass. One fails. The new check says the words "playwright install" must not appear anywhere in that job — but the job's own explanatory note ends with exactly those words, saying that no install is needed. The failure message points you at an install step that does not exist, so your first instinct is to go hunting for something that was never there.

verdicts.title: The first local shot run fails by design; the plan says to expect PASS
verdicts.section: Task 4 Step 4 (the landing shot) and Task 7 Step 3 (the Skeleton shot)
verdicts.contradicts: none. It reinforces F-7: both stem from Playwright writing local darwin PNGs into the committed snapshots folder. Neither Expected line's other claim changes — the darwin PNG is still written, and `git status --short` still shows no darwin PNG.
verdicts.spike: Ran it on @playwright/test 1.61.1 in a throwaway project under /private/tmp, with no updateSnapshots override (matching web/ and client/, neither of which sets one). Run 1, no baseline: FAILED, exit 1, "Error: A snapshot doesn't exist at …/brand-new-chromium-darwin.png, writing actual." — and the PNG was written. Run 2, same command: 1 passed. Run 3 with --retries=2 on a fresh missing baseline: '1 failed', no retry attempt at all, confirming the failure carries shouldNotRetryTest.
verdicts.whats_wrong: Both steps tell the implementer to expect PASS on a run where no baseline exists yet. Playwright's default updateSnapshots: 'missing' writes the file and then fails that attempt without retrying, so the run is red. Task 4 Step 4 is the plan's first end-to-end proof that the project split, the snapshot path and the container chain work, so a red there sends the implementer debugging a configuration that is correct.
verdicts.before:
Expected: PASS, having written `landing-chromium-darwin.png` (on a Mac). That file is git-ignored by
Task 1's line — confirm with `git status --short`, which must show **no** darwin PNG.

…

Expected: PASS. Open the written darwin PNG and confirm it shows the skeleton placeholder, **not**
rendered notation.
verdicts.after:
Expected: the shot FAILS once, with "A snapshot doesn't exist at …/landing-chromium-darwin.png,
writing actual." — measured on 1.61.1. That is Playwright's default `updateSnapshots: 'missing'`: it
writes the baseline and fails that attempt, without retrying. The darwin PNG is written all the same,

…

Expected: the first run FAILS with "A snapshot doesn't exist at …, writing actual." and writes the

verdicts.suggested_fix: Reword both Expected lines to say the first run fails once with "A snapshot doesn't exist at …, writing actual." while still writing the darwin PNG, and that a second run of the same command passes — which is the check that the shot is deterministic.
verdicts.why_it_works: It states the measured behaviour, so the implementer reads the red run as the documented first-run path instead of a broken config, and gains a second-run check that actually proves determinism.
verdicts.scenario: You write the first screenshot test and run it, and the plan says to expect a pass. It fails. There is no stored picture to compare against yet, so the tool saves one and reports the test as failed — that is how it is designed to behave. Because this run is the very first proof that your whole new setup works, a red result sends you hunting for a configuration mistake that is not there.

verdicts.title: The image-tag guard checks the shell helper by substring, not by exact pin
verdicts.section: Task 3, Step 3 — Write the failing image-tag guard
verdicts.contradicts: none, and specifically NOT the Task 9 container-pin assertion, which I checked as an overlapping pair: Task 9 asserts the web job HAS a pin of the right shape (/^\s+container: mcr\.microsoft\.com\/playwright:v[\d.]+-noble$/m, version left loose on purpose), while Task 3 asserts every pin EQUALS the installed version. They are complementary, they live in different tests, and this fix touches only the shell-script half, so no assertion about that literal changes meaning.
verdicts.spike: Extracted the prescribed helper from the plan and tested both forms. The proposed /^IMAGE=mcr\.microsoft\.com\/playwright:\S+$/gm matches exactly once today and equals the expected value, so the stronger guard passes as written; the literal appears exactly once in the helper, so nothing breaks now. I then simulated the drift case — a commented-out old line plus a new wrong pin: `.includes(expected)` returns true (guard stays GREEN on a wrong container), while the anchored form collects only 'IMAGE=…v1.60.0-noble' and fails. The weakness is durability, not a break the implementer hits.
verdicts.whats_wrong: The helper half of the guard passes as long as the expected tag appears anywhere in the file, including inside a comment or beside a second stale IMAGE assignment — so a partial bump can leave it green while the container actually used is a different Chromium. The same guard already treats ci.yml exhaustively one block later, and the plan's own standard forbids this unanchored shape for run lines.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Give the helper the same exhaustive treatment ci.yml gets: collect every anchored ^IMAGE=… line, assert at least one exists, and assert each equals `IMAGE=${expected}`.
verdicts.why_it_works: Spiked: the anchored form passes on the helper as written and fails the drift case the substring test lets through, so a partial version bump becomes all-or-nothing instead of silently comparing baselines under the wrong renderer.
verdicts.scenario: A year from now somebody upgrades the browser-testing tool and edits the shared script, leaving the old version line commented out just in case. The check that is meant to keep all three copies of the version number in step stays green, because it only asks whether the right text appears somewhere in the file — and it does, inside the comment. The pictures are then compared under a different browser build, and the failures look exactly like real design regressions.

verdicts.section: Task 9, Step 3 — Rename the `vr` artifact and its matching download (and Step 7's guard)
verdicts.contradicts: none. It adds one assertion to the same test file F-3 and F-4 touch, on a different subject; it neither reuses a bare substring (F-3's problem) nor an unanchored absence check (F-4's problem).
verdicts.spike: Verified every factual leg in .github/workflows/ci.yml: `playwright-vr-report` appears at line 238 (upload, inside the `vr` job) and line 272 (download, inside `vr-report`); the download step carries `continue-on-error: true` followed by a `[ -f ./vr-artifact/playwright-report/index.html ]` presence gate that makes the job succeed with present=false; and ci-green's needs list is [changes, quality, lint, build, a11y, vr, e2e, secret-scan, sast, deps-cve, pr-title, pr-checklist] — `vr-report` is absent. So a future one-sided rename is silent in all three respects. I also checked the fix is implementable: a `/^\s+name: playwright-\S+$/m` match hits only the artifact names, never a `- name:` step title.
verdicts.whats_wrong: The rename must land on both halves or the privileged vr-report job silently stops publishing, and nothing in the repo would ever go red: the download is continue-on-error, the presence gate turns a miss into success, and no job waits on vr-report. Task 8 rewrites this guard file's header to claim it pins every CI arrangement whose loss would be silent, and this one is not pinned.
verdicts.before: (absent — Task 9 Step 3 states the hazard in prose, "Two edits, and they must move together or `vr-report` silently stops finding the report it publishes", and adds no assertion for it)
verdicts.suggested_fix: In Task 9 Step 7, add one test that slices ci.yml to the `vr` and `vr-report` jobs, reads each block's artifact `name:` under its upload/download step, and asserts the two strings are equal.
verdicts.why_it_works: It turns the only thing holding the pair together — this PR's manual grep — into a check that survives the PR, so a future one-sided rename fails `pnpm run test:tooling` instead of quietly disarming the hosted diff page.
verdicts.scenario: Somebody later renames the report file on one side only — in the upload but not the matching download, or the reverse. The job that publishes the picture comparison to a web page quietly finds nothing, reports success, and nothing is waiting on it, so the whole repo stays green. The next person with a failed picture test gets no comparison page at all, and the fastest way out becomes accepting the new pictures without ever looking at them.

verdicts.title: lint:shell cannot see the new helper it is run to check
verdicts.section: Task 3, Step 6 — Lint the shell and commit
verdicts.spike: Verified the root script: "lint:shell": "git ls-files -z '*.sh' | xargs -0 -r shellcheck" — it enumerates tracked files only, so a brand-new untracked tooling/docker-playwright.sh is never passed to shellcheck. Same class of trap as the repo's own recorded lesson that linters walk the filesystem or the index, not your intent.
verdicts.whats_wrong: Step 6 runs pnpm run lint:shell before git add, and that script lists tracked files only, so the one file this task creates is never checked. The step goes green having linted every other shell script in the repo, and the plan's "shellcheck-clean" claim is unverified at the only point it is checked.
verdicts.before:
```bash
pnpm run lint:shell && pnpm run lint:sort-pkg && pnpm run test:tooling
```

```bash
git add tooling/docker-playwright.sh package.json tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs
git commit -m "test: share one Playwright container invocation across client and web (NH-320)"
```
verdicts.after:
Stage first: `lint:shell` is `git ls-files -z '*.sh' | xargs -0 -r shellcheck`, so it enumerates
TRACKED files only and would skip the brand-new helper entirely.

```bash
git add tooling/docker-playwright.sh package.json tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs
pnpm run lint:shell && pnpm run lint:sort-pkg && pnpm run test:tooling
```

```bash
git commit -m "test: share one Playwright container invocation across client and web (NH-320)"
```
verdicts.suggested_fix: Swap the order in Step 6 — git add the three files first, then run lint:shell / lint:sort-pkg / test:tooling, then commit — and say in one line why (lint:shell reads git ls-files).
verdicts.why_it_works: Once the file is staged, git ls-files enumerates it, so shellcheck actually reads the new helper at the point the plan claims it does.
verdicts.scenario: You create the new shared script, then run the shell-script checker exactly where the plan tells you to, and it passes. It never looked at your file: the checker only reads files that git already tracks, and yours is brand new. You commit believing it was checked, and only find out otherwise when the same check runs somewhere else.

verdicts.title: The standalone probe recipe discards uncommitted edits with no stated precondition
verdicts.section: The one hazard outside the spec's footprint — measured, and fixed in Task 4 (and the same recipe in Task 4 Step 2)
verdicts.spike: Untested by design — I will not run a recipe whose last line is `git checkout -- web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts` inside the worktree, and I was asked not to modify repo files. Verified by reading: the block appends to web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts and ends in an unconditional checkout of that file, which Task 2 rewrites at nine call sites; and the block is presented as a self-contained reproduction with no precondition.
verdicts.whats_wrong: Anyone re-running the reproduction out of task order loses any uncommitted work in web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts, because the recipe ends in an unconditional git checkout of a file this plan itself rewrites heavily. A build failure between the printf and the checkout also leaves the planted comment in the working tree with no later git add that would surface it.
verdicts.before:
```bash
printf '\n// mt-[137px]\n' >> web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts
pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web run build
grep -rl 'mt-\[137px\]' web/.next/static/ --include='*.css'   # prints the emitted chunk
git checkout -- web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts
```
verdicts.after:
Precondition: `git diff --quiet -- web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts` must pass before you run this. The last line
discards that file's working-tree state, and Task 2 rewrites it at nine call sites — so run this only
with that file clean. If the build fails mid-way, the planted comment is still in the working tree;
run the last line by hand.

```bash
git diff --quiet -- web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts || { echo 'a11y.e2e.ts has uncommitted changes — commit or stash first'; exit 1; }
printf '\n// mt-[137px]\n' >> web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts
pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web run build
grep -rl 'mt-\[137px\]' web/.next/static/ --include='*.css'   # prints the emitted chunk
git checkout -- web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts
```
verdicts.suggested_fix: Preface the reproduction block with a git diff --quiet guard on web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts and a one-line note that the last line discards that file's working-tree state, and state the same precondition in Task 4 Step 2.
verdicts.why_it_works: The recipe then refuses to run against a dirty copy of the one file it destroys, so re-running it out of order cannot cost work.
verdicts.scenario: You want to see the measurement behind one of the plan's claims, so you copy the four-line recipe from the bottom of the document and run it. Its last line throws away every uncommitted change in one of the test files — the same file the plan rewrites in nine places earlier on. If you happened to have unsaved work there, it is gone, and nothing in the recipe warned you that it does that.

verdicts.title: The header wordmark's sub-md collapse is covered by no shot and named by no note
verdicts.spike: Verified web/app/play/PlayerHeader.tsx:153 carries `max-md:sr-only` on the wordmark span, and that both shot widths (1280 px and the narrow 900 px) sit above Tailwind's md (768 px), so no shot ever renders the collapsed header. Also verified the plan's Task 6 Step 3 comment names only the 640 px transport-footer gap.
verdicts.whats_wrong: No shot renders the header below 768 px, where the product name is hidden and the remaining controls must fit. The plan explicitly reasons through the sibling gap one breakpoint over (the transport footer at 640 px) but says nothing about this symmetric header gap, so a reader cannot tell whether it was considered and excluded on the same grounds or simply missed.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Widen the existing uncovered-breakpoint comment in Task 6 Step 3 to name both gaps — the transport footer's 640 px step and the header wordmark's max-md:sr-only collapse at 768 px — under the same "desktop web is the v0 target" reason.
verdicts.why_it_works: It costs one sentence and makes the second gap read as a decision rather than an oversight, which is the only thing separating them today.
verdicts.scenario: Someone later breaks the layout of the player's top bar at narrow widths, where the product name is hidden and the remaining controls have to squeeze together. None of the nine pictures notices, because even the narrowest one is still fairly wide. The plan carefully explains one other width it chose not to cover, so a reader naturally assumes anything it does not mention is covered.

dedup_notes: Three clusters merged as instructed. F-1 = adversarial 'Rail and footer surface assertions pass against transparent parent' + design-lens 'Rail/footer surface checks compare against a transparent parent' + feasibility 'Surface assertions compare against transparent parents' — one entry at P1 (all three were already P1); all three diagnose the same transparent-parent mechanism and all three point at Task 5 Steps 3 and 5, but they proposed THREE different fixes (document.body twice, nearest-painting-ancestor-plus-rename once), so the merge had to pick one — see cross_fix_conflicts. F-4 = adversarial 'Web-job guard forbids a phrase the job's own comment carries' (P1) + feasibility 'web-job guard rejects its own explanatory comment' (P2) — one entry at P1, the higher of the two, identical diagnosis and effectively identical fix. F-5 = adversarial 'First local shot run fails by design, not PASS' + feasibility 'First VR run fails, not passes, on a missing snapshot' — one entry at P2, same two Expected lines, same mechanism; feasibility added the library-internal detail (handleMissing / shouldNotRetryTest) that my spike confirmed behaviourally. Everything else is single-reviewer and kept at its filed severity. coherence-reviewer filed ZERO findings; its residual risks overlap F-3 (it independently noticed the Task 8 guard is a string-presence check) and its deferred question 2 asks exactly what F-3 answers — worth telling the user that two reviewers reached the same doubt, one as a finding and one as a question.
cross_fix_conflicts:
Test 3 turned up one real conflict, one incomplete fix and one self-contradiction, all three inside the clusters named in the brief.

1. REAL CONFLICT, inside cluster F-1, between reviewers. design-lens and adversarial both fix surfaceDiffersFromParent by comparing against document.body and KEEP the helper's name. feasibility fixes it by walking up to the nearest painting ancestor and RENAMING the helper to surfaceDiffersFromBackdrop. Either works today (the walk terminates at body, since nothing between paints), but the rename collides with F-3's fix, whose first two anchors were proposed as /surfaceDiffersFromParent\(page, 'player-rail'\)/: apply feasibility's rename and F-3's guard matches nothing, so `pnpm run test:tooling` fails on the very assertion meant to protect the shots. I resolved it two ways at once — F-1 takes the document.body form the orchestrator already spiked (simpler, and not fragile against a future painted wrapper, which adversarial itself flagged as a residual risk), and F-3's anchors are written helper-name-agnostic as `(page, 'player-rail')`, verified to match the assertion, to survive any rename, and to match none of the false positives (the snapshot filename, a bare getByTestId, a prose comment). The two fixes are now independent in either order.

2. INCOMPLETE FIX, inside the F-1/F-2 pair. The brief asked whether a fix to one implies a different fix to the other: it does, and not in the direction adversarial proposed. adversarial's F-2 fix (compare the hovered value against the RAIL's background, mirroring its F-1 fix) does NOT catch hover:bg-elevate reverting to hover:bg-muted — the exact regression the shot's own comment names — because --muted differs from --rail. I spiked all three candidates in Chromium: the 'differs from something' shape cannot work for the ghost hover at all, because that step is a change between two NON-transparent values rather than a surface being present or absent. So the two assertions genuinely need different shapes: F-1 keeps 'differs from the page background', F-2 becomes 'equals --elevate, read through the same serializer'. That is consistent with, not contrary to, the plan's own rule in the Task 5 helper doc-comment that both values must go through one serializer — and it is why I did NOT unify them into one helper.

3. SELF-CONTRADICTION in F-8 as filed. feasibility's fix adds web/README.md to the plan's Modified list, but web/README.md is not in the spec's 'Process changes this carries' list (grepped — the spec names client/README.md only), so the fix silently creates a SECOND out-of-footprint file against the plan's own line 148 ('One file sits outside the spec's stated footprint') and the matching single-file PR-body bullet. Confirmed with the fix extended to update both places.

4. Cluster 3 checked and CLEAN. The Task 3 image-tag guard (F-11) and the Task 9 container-pin assertion do assert about the same literal, but they do not conflict: Task 9 asserts, scoped to the web job, that a pin of the right SHAPE exists (version deliberately loose, /v[\d.]+-noble/), while Task 3 asserts every pin in ci.yml EQUALS the version derived from @playwright/test. F-11's fix touches only the shell-script half, adds no ci.yml assertion, and I verified the strengthened regex passes against the helper exactly as the plan prescribes it. F-3's and F-4's fixes are likewise mutually consistent — both replace a bare substring with an anchored construct, and they pull in the same direction (F-3 is a presence check that prose must not satisfy; F-4 is an absence check that prose must not trip), so neither reintroduces the other's problem. F-12 adds a third assertion to the same file on a different subject, using the same anchoring discipline.
notes:
All 24 evidence quotes across all 15 findings are VERBATIM — checked by exact substring search against the plan, not by eye (script at /private/tmp/verify-nh320/check-quotes.mjs). Every cited section exists. Nothing was DROPPED: 15 CONFIRMED, 0 DROPPED.

The three commissioned spikes all came back in favour of the findings, and two of them also corrected a reviewer's proposed fix — see cross_fix_conflicts items 1 and 2. Spike artifacts are under /private/tmp/verify-nh320/ (throwaway Playwright project in spike/, guard replay in spike3.mjs, regex checks in fixcheck.mjs). Nothing in the repo was modified.

Two things the orchestrator should know that are NOT findings, because no reviewer filed them and I did not widen scope:

(a) Spike 1's result ripples further than the two steps F-5 names. Task 6 Step 5 tells the implementer to run the narrow-rail shot and 'Expected: 80' — that run is also a red run, because no darwin baseline exists for player-narrow yet; the console.log still prints 80, so the step's own check survives, but the run status will look wrong for the same reason as F-5. Worth folding into F-5's edit if the user applies it.

(b) The plan's THIRD colour assertion — Task 5's tempo-percent opacity poll — is sound. It compares a computed opacity against the literal '1', not against another element, so it does not share F-1's or F-2's defect. I checked it rather than assume.

On severity weighting for the walk-through: F-1 through F-4 are all P1 and all four break a step the plan tells the implementer to run and expect a specific result from, so each one costs a debugging cycle at a different point in the task list (Task 5, Task 6, Task 8, Task 9). F-1, F-2 and F-3 additionally compound: F-3 is the guard meant to protect the assertions F-1 and F-2 fix, so applying F-3 alone would pin two assertions that cannot fail.

One carried-forward caveat on F-1's severity, raised by design-lens as a residual risk and not measured by anyone: nobody has scored --rail against --background or --panel against --background on the 1408.6 per-pixel cutoff. If those steps happen to clear it, the screenshot alone would still catch a bg-rail-to-bg-background regression, which would soften F-1's real-world impact without changing that the assertion is non-functional as written. It does not change the fix.
